cards.title: Familiarize with QP-CRM codebase and architecture
cards.description: Read all 4 docs (README_API/FEATURES/PROGRAM_DOCUMENTATION/API_INSTRUCTIONS), main.py, every module's routes/schema, and AUDIT_FINDINGS.md. Verified vs code this pass: 6 sub-apps merged via DispatcherMiddleware on :5000 + /api/v1 blueprint; single SQLite app_data/pricing.db (WAL) with ~16 tables incl. site_products (WP sync snapshot); module-level WeasyPrint imports (offer/app.py:8, rent/app.py:10) are the known boot blocker (missing libpango, needs root). NEW vs prior pass: undocumented site-sync feature (pricing/templates/product_sync.html + /api/v1/sync/{fetch,table,link,unlink,product_info,add_product} pulling from autoservisnaoprema.com WP REST API, 1:1 products.site_product_id link); rent lease calculator replicates Excel PMT; 'System Default' PDF template re-synced from filesystem at every admin boot; AUDIT_FINDINGS.md tracks C1-C5/H1-H10/M1-M11 issues (SSTI via stored PDF templates, no CSRF except settings app, plaintext passwords).
cards.summary: Re-surveyed docs + all 7 packages' entry points, route maps, DB schema (all CREATE TABLE blocks), rent PMT calculator, offer recalc_totals cascade, sync API, deploy scripts; wrote architecture summary for the user.
cards.rationale: Goal 1 of the session request — understand the app before running it; needed to predict the WeasyPrint boot blocker (module-level imports in offer/app.py:8 and rent/app.py:10).
cards.rejected: Skimming every route in the 1.2-1.8k-line app.py files — PROGRAM_DOCUMENTATION.md already enumerates all routes per module with implementation notes, so per-route reading was redundant for setup purposes.

cards.title: Set up QP-CRM Python environment (venv + deps)
cards.description: run_apps.sh aborted at its sudo apt step (sandbox: "no new privileges" flag blocks sudo; set -e killed the script), so app_data/, venv/ and pip install never ran from the script. Manual fallback: mkdir -p app_data/product_images; python3 -m venv failed because ensurepip/python3.12-venv is missing and there is no system pip3; recreated with `python3 -m venv --without-pip venv` + curl get-pip.py bootstrap; installed requirements.txt (Flask 3.1.3, Pillow 12.3.0, requests, WeasyPrint 69.0, pypdf 6.16.2, python-docx 1.2.0, mammoth 1.12.1, lxml 6.1.3) + Werkzeug 3.1.8. Note: `markdown` is intentionally NOT a pip dep — it is vendored in custom_libs/ and added to sys.path at runtime by the sub-apps.
cards.summary: Created app_data/product_images, venv (get-pip.py bootstrap since ensurepip missing), all requirements + Werkzeug installed and verified importable.
cards.rationale: Goal 2 prerequisite — the app cannot run without its Python dependencies; the sanctioned fallback path when run_apps.sh's apt step aborts.
cards.rejected: Editing run_apps.sh to skip the apt block — task said run it as-is and only do remaining steps manually; also rejected --system-site-packages venv (nothing useful installed system-side anyway).

cards.title: Phase 0 — Dockerize QP-CRM (image + compose + volumes + env secrets)
cards.description: PHASE 0 of the roadmap (first execution phase; runs in a dedicated chat). Dockerize for easy running/updating of the main instance. Steps: (1) pin requirements (pip freeze from working venv) + add gunicorn; (2) wsgi entrypoint `from main import application` + explicit init sequence (pricing_init_db, pricing_migrate_schema, offer_init_db, admin_init_db, rent_init_db) since those run only under `__main__` today; (3) Dockerfile python:3.12-slim + apt libs from run_apps.sh PKGS list (libpango-1.0-0 libpangoft2-1.0-0 libharfbuzz-subset0 libgdk-pixbuf-2.0-0 libcairo2 shared-mime-info fonts-dejavu-core) — also fixes the current libpango boot blocker on this machine; non-root user; gunicorn --workers 2 --threads 4 (debugger/reloader OFF, audit C1); switch pricing/offer/rent hardcoded secret keys to os.environ.get; (4) docker-compose.yml: volumes app_data/ + app_assets/ + static/img (logo upload writes into static/img — lost on rebuild without a volume), env-based secrets, TZ=Europe/Belgrade, healthcheck /api/v1/health, restart unless-stopped; (5) .dockerignore (venv, .git, README_Images, *.pdf, *.xlsx, main.log, scratch scripts); (6) smoke checklist: login each app, product+price, offer PDF, rent doc PDF, backup download; (7) replace run_apps.sh git-pull/pkill -f main.py update flow with image rebuild (audit M11); keep run_apps.sh for bare-metal users. HANDOVER PROTOCOL on completion: commit per step on a phase branch, tag the image, mark this card done with summary+rejected fields, write an Agent Note for the dockerization decisions — the next phase chat starts from the board.
cards.rationale: User confirmed the per-phase dedicated-chat workflow; the docker card is the entry point of the whole roadmap and must carry an explicit phase number and the handover protocol so a fresh chat with zero conversation memory can execute it from the board alone.
cards.rejected: Alpine base (musl breaks WeasyPrint), named volumes (bind mounts reuse host data, uid 1000 matches), schema creation at build time (data belongs in volumes), random token_hex secret fallbacks (invalidate sessions per restart — stable old literals kept as dev fallback), subagent-written Dockerfile (3 stall attempts — orchestrator wrote it directly).
cards.summary: PHASE 0 COMPLETE on branch phase-0-docker (git tag phase-0), image qp-crm:phase0 (382MB), stack healthy. Executed via 8 task cards (P0-T1..T8) + 9 per-step commits: pinned requirements+gunicorn 26.2.0 (61080f1); wsgi.py entrypoint replaying main.py's init sequence fork-safely (cda297d); Dockerfile python:3.12-slim + WeasyPrint libs + non-root uid 1000 + gunicorn --preload (273826d + perms fix 867ca19); compose stack with bind-mount volumes (app_data/app_assets/static/img), env_file .env, TZ=Europe/Belgrade, restart unless-stopped, /api/v1/health healthcheck (f5196da); deploy.sh rebuild-and-wait flow + DOCKER.md, run_apps.sh kept for bare metal (1bd588d); custom_libs tracked for fresh-clone builds (3592f80). Smoke checklist ALL PASS: health, 4 app logins, product+price via UI, offer PDF (SMOKE-2026-001, 386KB), rent doc PDF (44.5KB), backup download (SQLite 221KB). .env with real generated secrets on host (git-ignored, chmod 600); .env.example checked in. Dev branch untouched.

cards.title: Phase 3 — Users & user management (unified auth, roles, CSRF, hashing)
cards.description: Phase 3 of the roadmap — ran AFTER Phase 2 (single app + blueprints) so login/session/CSRF were written once against the final shape. Env-based secrets for Docker landed in Phase 0 (pricing/offer/rent hardcoded keys switched to os.environ.get there). Delivered: users table (id, username, password_hash, role, is_active, modules_set, created_at, last_login); single unified login on the top-level app (one qp_session cookie, path=/, 8h sliding expiry); per-app password gates replaced by shared require_role('admin'/'staff') + per-user app access via require_module and the user_modules table (pricing/offer/rent/sale checkboxes per staff user in Admin -> Users; admins bypass); werkzeug hashed passwords with transparent rehash-on-login from legacy plaintext (no plaintext at rest — scrub_legacy_password_keys on every boot); CSRF shield on every state-changing route incl. AJAX (settings-app pattern generalized into shared/web.py; audit C5 closed); API keys table + per-user keys with attribution (global key deprecated but working); login_audit log + in-process lockout (5 fails / 15 min per IP+username); sandboxed Jinja for DB PDF templates already closed C4 in Phase 2, template editor admin-only; Admin Users UI (create/deactivate/reset/role change, one Save per user, own-password confirmed), landing page requires login + access-filtered app menu, logout moved into Settings, header unified with Home button. Extra user-request UX work folded in (Serbian feedback cards): admin header options missing on subpages fixed via shared _nav include, /admin/rent/templates login loop fixed, logout button moved to settings, Landing Page renamed Home. Suite grew to 243+ tests; 3 golden-PDF skips outside the pinned image by design. Verified live on :5000 (admin walks all module pages, anonymous redirects to /login?next=, CSRF 400s on tokenless POSTs, /api/v1 401 without key).
cards.rationale: User's milestone 2, positioned after the Phase-2 blueprint consolidation so login/session/CSRF were written once against the final shape and before features (roles gate who may create invoices, edit stock, manage templates).
cards.rejected: Heavy auth frameworks (Flask-User/OAuth) — overkill for LAN scale; per-app user tables — would perpetuate the six-realm session split; landing auth before consolidation — double work. Forced first-login password change — retired mid-phase by user request (password changes exclusively admin-managed in Admin -> Users); default staff users kept as seeds — retired later by the 'no default users beyond admin' change (separate card/commit 4f3a2a1).
cards.summary: Phase 3 delivered and verified: unified login + roles + per-user module grants, werkzeug hashing with legacy rehash + scrub, CSRF everywhere, per-user API keys + audit, lockout, 8h sessions, Admin Users UI, landing auth gate + access-filtered menu, and the user-requested header/logout/Home fixes. Exit criteria met (single login, roles enforced per module, every POST CSRF-protected, no plaintext at rest).

cards.title: Phase 1 — Test safety net: characterization + golden-PDF tests (before any refactor)
cards.description: Prerequisite for ALL structural work: the app has zero tests, so 'clear technical debt' without this is gambling with the price engine. Build a small, high-value pytest suite: (1) characterization tests for pure business logic — recalc_totals 3-level discount cascade, apply_rounding + rounding rules, calculate_rent/pmt/generate_schedule, format_amount/format_date, rent placeholder substitution; (2) golden-file PDF tests — render one fixed offer and one fixed rent document, compare against checked-in baselines (pin fonts in the image for byte-stability), re-baselined consciously only when a change is intended; (3) Flask test-client smoke tests per module (login → main pages → 200). Runs via `docker compose run app pytest`; wire into CI if a repo host exists. Exit criteria: suite green on main; every Phase-2 refactor step must keep it green.
cards.rationale: User's plan is to break the monolith and clear tech debt before features. Refactoring an untested price/lease/discount engine silently changes money — the safety net must exist before the first structural commit, and it is what makes 'time is no object' refactoring safe instead of brave.
cards.rejected: Host-venv test runs (WeasyPrint unimportable without libpango); compose-override test service (breaks the one plain command); fixing discovered bugs (forbidden — they are Phase-2 cards now); pushing to origin (user decides).
cards.summary: DONE. Suite: 120 tests green on the UNMODIFIED app — 4 infra guards, 33 rounding, 6 recalc cascade, 22 rent math, 29 formatting+placeholders, 2 golden PDFs, 24 smoke. ONE command (documented on this card, in tests/README.md and DOCKER.md): docker compose build app && docker compose run --rm app pytest. Suite runs INSIDE the pinned image (fonts pinned, no host deps), fully isolated from the real app_data (throwaway /tmp/qp-crm-tests, guarded by tests/test_infra_isolation.py). Golden-PDF baselines for one fixed offer + one fixed rent document are checked in and byte-stable across containers (normalizer blanks PDF dates/trailer /ID only). Branch phase-1-tests (7+1 commits, per-step), image qp-crm:phase1 (phase0 = rollback), stack healthy. Characterization captured quirks AS-IS; 5 bug cards tagged bug/phase-2-candidate; zero production-code changes (test plumbing only: dev-requirements layer, .dockerignore, compose image tag, docs).

cards.title: Phase 2 — Structural refactor: single app + blueprints, single schema, service layer
cards.description: The monolith-breaking program, done incrementally with Phase-1 tests green at every step and a Docker image rebuild + smoke test per merged step. Order within the phase: (1) consolidate 6 Flask instances → 1 Flask app + blueprints, URL prefixes preserved (/pricing, /offer, /rent, /admin, /sale, /settings), one session/secret/cookie, remove DispatcherMiddleware — validate the pattern on the smallest module (sale or settings) first, then pricing/offer/rent/admin; (2) deduplicate copy-pasted helpers (md filter, format_date, get_theme, check_auth → blueprint-level hooks) into shared/; (3) single-source the DB schema — one schema module consumed by all init_db calls, delete the stale offers/offer_items duplicate in pricing/app.py, keep idempotent ALTER migrations, add UNIQUE constraints where data permits; (4) extract service layer — pricing_service (cascade+rounding), offer_service (totals+numbering), rent_service (PMT+schedule+placeholders), pdf_service (shared WeasyPrint render helper with sandboxed Jinja → fixes SSTI during the move); (5) split 1.2–1.8k-line route files into per-domain modules; (6) proper package layout (qp_crm/), delete sys.path hacks, replace vendored custom_libs/markdown with pinned pip dependency Markdown==3.10.2; (7) CI running pytest. DISCIPLINE: zero behavior changes inside this phase — same URLs, same totals, byte-comparable PDFs; improvements go to the Phase-4 backlog. Exit criteria: single app, no DispatcherMiddleware, no sys.path hacks, no vendored libs, single schema source, tests green.
cards.rationale: Phase 2's contract was structural-only: make the codebase testable and safe without changing user-visible behavior (golden PDFs byte-identical), then fix the pinned bugs deliberately with referenced re-baselines. Delivered so the user can manually test before Phase 3 (users/auth/CSRF).
cards.rejected: Big-bang rewrite: rejected from the start (see architecture-direction card). Bundle-fixing the 5 bugs during the structural stages was also rejected — zero-behavior-change discipline during 1-6 kept every green suite a real regression gate; bugs were fixed only after the structure was byte-verified. Remaining known debt deliberately deferred to Phase 3+: H10 bare-numeric input validation, L9 fresh connection per call, L11 float money -> Decimal, bracket-selection product decision.
cards.summary: All 7 structural stages shipped on branch phase-2-refactor (single app+blueprints, shared/ dedupe, single schema, service layer + sandboxed Jinja closing audit C4, per-domain route modules, qp_crm/ package with sys.path hacks deleted and Markdown==3.10.2 devendored, GH Actions CI), then all 5 phase-2-candidate BUG cards fixed with one commit + regression test each (rent pmt zero-period, rent schedule bad-date 400, offer discount normalization, pricing rounding semantics decision, sale bare-schema empty state). Exit criteria met: single app, no DispatcherMiddleware, no sys.path hacks, no vendored libs, single schema source. Suite 133 passed; image tagged qp-crm:phase2 (docker-compose.yml + DOCKER.md updated); golden PDFs byte-identical throughout stages 1-6.

cards.title: P0-T1 · Pin requirements.txt from working venv + add gunicorn
cards.description: Step 1 of the Phase-0 card. Install gunicorn into the existing venv, then `venv/bin/pip freeze` and rewrite requirements.txt with exact pins. Keep a comment noting: `markdown` is intentionally NOT a pip dep — vendored in custom_libs/ and added to sys.path at runtime (Phase 2 replaces this).
cards.rationale: Reproducible image builds require exact versions; unpinned ranges would make rebuilds drift and later break Phase-1 golden-PDF baselines for non-code reasons.
cards.rejected: constraints file + loose top-level requirements — overkill for a single-image app; one pinned file is what the Dockerfile consumes.
cards.summary: requirements.txt rewritten from venv pip freeze: 30 exact pins incl. gunicorn==26.2.0, Flask==3.1.3, weasyprint==69.0, Werkzeug==3.1.8; header documents the freeze procedure and that 'markdown' stays vendored in custom_libs (3.10.2) until Phase 2. pip check: no broken requirements. Committed as 'P0 step 1'.

cards.title: P0-T2 · wsgi.py entrypoint + explicit DB init sequence
cards.description: Step 2. Create /home/dsh/QP-CRM/wsgi.py exposing `application` and running the init sequence (pricing_init_db → pricing_migrate_schema → offer_init_db → admin_init_db → rent_init_db — exact names verified from main.py) at import, ensuring app_data dirs exist and no SQLite connection stays open across gunicorn fork.
cards.rationale: Schema init ran only under main.py's __main__ block; gunicorn never triggers it, so a fresh volume would boot with no schema. Init at wsgi import makes any WSGI server boot self-initializing and idempotent (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS + guarded ALTERs).
cards.rejected: Schema creation at docker build time — data must live in volumes, created at runtime; try/except around init — silent empty-schema boots are worse than loud crashes; per-worker init without --preload — works (20s busy timeout) but --preload makes init run exactly once in the master, adopted in the Dockerfile CMD.
cards.summary: Created wsgi.py: sys.path root insert, os.makedirs for APP_DATA_DIR/IMAGE_DIR/APP_ASSETS_DIR before imports, explicit init sequence pricing_init_db → pricing_migrate_schema → offer_init_db → admin_init_db → rent_init_db (verified same order + same source modules as main.py:66-70), then 'from main import application' (DispatcherMiddleware, main.py:52-59). No try/except around init — boot fails loud. Connection audit: no module-level sqlite connections anywhere (all function-local, init paths close before return) → fork-safe. Committed as 'P0 step 2'.

cards.title: P0-T3 · Dockerfile: python:3.12-slim + WeasyPrint libs + non-root + gunicorn
cards.description: Step 3. python:3.12-slim base; apt packages from run_apps.sh PKGS (libpango-1.0-0 libpangoft2-1.0-0 libharfbuzz-subset0 libgdk-pixbuf-2.0-0 libcairo2 shared-mime-info fonts-dejavu-core) + tzdata — also fixes the host libpango boot blocker; WORKDIR /app; pip install -r requirements.txt; non-root uid/gid 1000 (matches host dsh uid for bind mounts); ENV TZ=Europe/Belgrade PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1; EXPOSE 5000; CMD gunicorn --workers 2 --threads 4 --bind 0.0.0.0:5000 wsgi:application (debugger/reloader OFF — audit C1). custom_libs/ MUST be copied (vendored markdown needed at runtime).
cards.rationale: The proven WeasyPrint lib set + slim base keeps PDF rendering working in a small image; uid 1000 matches the host owner of the compose bind mounts; --preload makes wsgi.py's init run exactly once in the master (T2 connection audit: no global conns, fork-safe).
cards.rejected: Alpine — musl breaks WeasyPrint/pango wheels; python:3.12 full — 1GB+ for nothing; root container — bind-mount permission mismatch; per-worker init without --preload — idempotent but races ALTER TABLE migrations on cold volumes.
cards.summary: Dockerfile written by orchestrator (3 subagent attempts stalled): python:3.12-slim + apt PKGS from run_apps.sh (libpango, libpangoft2, libharfbuzz-subset0, libgdk-pixbuf, libcairo2, shared-mime-info, fonts-dejavu-core) + tzdata; ENV TZ=Europe/Belgrade; requirements layer cached; COPY . . incl. custom_libs; non-root appuser uid/gid 1000 with chown on data dirs only; gunicorn --workers 2 --threads 4 --preload --bind 0.0.0.0:5000 wsgi:application, reloader OFF (audit C1). Committed as 'P0 step 3'.

cards.title: P0-T4 · Env-based secret keys in pricing/offer/rent
cards.description: Step 3 security slice. Replace hardcoded `app.secret_key = "crm_*_secret_key_change_me"` in pricing/app.py, offer/app.py, rent/app.py with `os.environ.get("PRICING_SECRET_KEY"/"OFFER_SECRET_KEY"/"RENT_SECRET_KEY", <old literal as dev fallback>)`, mirroring the existing admin/app.py pattern. settings/sale/admin are already env-aware — no change.
cards.rationale: Image-baked identical secret keys across installs violate the Phase-0 env-secrets requirement (audit); compose injects real values via .env while the old literal keeps bare-metal dev behavior unchanged.
cards.rejected: Random token_hex fallback (settings/app.py style) — would invalidate sessions on every restart; env-var-with-stable-fallback chosen instead.
cards.summary: Replaced hardcoded crm_*_secret_key_change_me in pricing/app.py, offer/app.py, rent/app.py with os.environ.get('PRICING|OFFER|RENT_SECRET_KEY', <old literal>), mirroring admin/app.py; committed as 'P0 step 3 (secrets)'.

cards.title: P0-T5 · docker-compose.yml + .dockerignore
cards.description: Steps 4+5. Compose: build ., image qp-crm:phase0, port 5000:5000, bind mounts ./app_data ./app_assets ./static/img (logo upload writes into static/img — lost on rebuild without the volume), env_file .env, TZ=Europe/Belgrade, restart unless-stopped, healthcheck on /api/v1/health via python urllib (no curl in slim). .dockerignore: venv, .git, .agents, KANBAN.json, README_Images, *.pdf, *.xlsx, *.xlsb, logs, scratch scripts (download_pdf*, measure_pdf*, test_*), app_data/, .env — but NOT custom_libs/.
cards.rationale: Volumes keep all mutable state outside the image so rebuilds never lose data (card step 4); .dockerignore keeps secrets, DBs and scratch files out of image layers (step 5).
cards.rejected: Named volumes — bind mounts reuse existing host data and stay inspectable; curl in image for healthcheck — python stdlib is already present; obsolete compose version: key — removed per Compose v2.
cards.summary: docker-compose.yml (qp-crm:phase0, port 5000, env_file .env, TZ=Europe/Belgrade, bind mounts app_data/app_assets/static/img, restart unless-stopped, python-stdlib healthcheck on /api/v1/health with 60s start_period), .dockerignore (venv/.git/app_data/.env/scratch junk with **/ depth variants; custom_libs deliberately NOT ignored), .env.example (six secret keys + generation hint). Verified with docker compose config.

cards.title: P0-T6 · deploy.sh: image-rebuild update flow (replaces run_apps.sh update path, audit M11)
cards.description: Step 7. New deploy.sh: docker compose build → up -d → wait for /api/v1/health → show ps/logs. run_apps.sh stays untouched for bare-metal users. Short DOCKER.md documenting first run, update flow, volumes, backups.
cards.rationale: Replaces the run_apps.sh git-pull/pkill -f main.py update flow (audit M11) with image rebuild + recreate; data safety comes from the bind mounts.
cards.rejected: Editing run_apps.sh to auto-detect Docker — one script doing two jobs is unclear and the card says keep it for bare-metal; requiring --ff-only pull success — offline/diverged deploys should still proceed with a warning.
cards.summary: deploy.sh (git pull --ff-only non-fatal → docker compose build → up -d → ~90s health poll via docker inspect, fail-fast on unhealthy with log dump) + DOCKER.md ops doc (first run, update, volumes, backups incl. WAL stop-and-copy warning, logs). run_apps.sh left untouched for bare-metal users. Committed per step.

cards.title: P0-T7 · Build image + compose up + automated smoke checklist
cards.description: Step 6 smoke list, automated as far as curl allows: docker compose build, up -d, healthcheck green; login each app (creds discovered from code/docs), pricing product+price flow, offer PDF render (non-empty %PDF bytes), rent doc PDF, admin backup download; report per-item PASS/FAIL. Requires T1–T6 merged and Docker installed. RUN TWICE — both runs fully green (agent re-executed all form flows on request).
cards.rationale: Automating the phase-card smoke list proves the image is genuinely runnable before manual user testing; the offer/rent PDF checks additionally prove WeasyPrint works in-container (the host libpango blocker is bypassed entirely).
cards.rejected: Selenium UI checks — curl/form-level POSTs cover the checklist; deeper UI testing stays with the user's manual pass.
cards.summary: All 6 smoke items PASS — verified in TWO independent runs. (1) /api/v1/health → {success:true} + Docker healthcheck healthy in ~7s. (2) Logins admin/pricing/offer/rent (Admin1/Price1/Offer1/Rent1) → dashboards render. (3) Product via API + prices via UI (run1 final 14500.00/disc 13790.00; run2 final 14900.00/disc 14155.00). (4) Offer PDFs SMOKE-2026-001 + SMOKE-2026-002: %PDF-1.7, ~386KB each. (5) Rent doc PDFs Prilog_4_Plan_Placanja_010926/020926.pdf: %PDF-1.7, ~44.5KB — WeasyPrint renders in-container. (6) /admin/backup_db: 221,184 bytes, SQLite magic. deploy.sh exercised end-to-end twice incl. one failure+fix cycle (mode-600 COPY → chmod a+rX fix, 867ca19). TEST DATA NOW IN DB (runs 1+2): 2 price rows on product 1, offers SMOKE-2026-001/002 (+1 item each), 2 rent clients, 2 equipment, 2 contracts (010926, 020926) — user should delete/ignore before real use.

cards.title: P0-T8 · Handover: commits per step, image tag, board + Agent Note
cards.description: Commit each task's files separately on phase-0-docker with step-numbered messages; tag image qp-crm:phase0; mark the parent Phase-0 card done with summary+rejected; write the Agent Note for dockerization decisions; leave Dev untouched.
cards.rationale: The parent card's handover protocol requires a tagged, rollback-able phase end state and a durable decision record so a fresh chat with zero conversation memory can continue from the board alone.

cards.summary: Handover protocol executed: 9 per-step commits on phase-0-docker (step-numbered messages), git tag phase-0, image tagged qp-crm:phase0, parent card closed with summary+rejected, Agent Note 'qp-crm-dockerization' written under .agents/notes/implemented/feature/. Next phase chat starts from the board.

cards.title: P1-T1 · pytest infra: branch, dev-requirements, Dockerfile test layer, .dockerignore, pytest.ini, conftest isolation, one-command run
cards.description: Step 1 of the Phase-1 card. Branch phase-1-tests from phase-0-docker tip (origin REACHABLE, so Dev is left untouched per instructions). dev-requirements.txt with pinned pytest; Dockerfile installs it as a separate layer so production requirements.txt stays untouched; .dockerignore must NOT exclude tests/ (blanket test_*.py rule replaced by the named root scratch scripts, tests/** re-included so golden PDF baselines ship in the image); compose image bumped to qp-crm:phase1 (qp-crm:phase0 kept as rollback tag); pytest.ini with testpaths=tests (root scratch test_*.py files must never be collected) and cache_dir=/tmp (/app is read-only for appuser); tests/conftest.py patches shared.config APP_DATA_DIR/DATABASE/IMAGE_DIR/APP_ASSETS_DIR into a throwaway temp dir BEFORE any app module is imported (every module binds those names at import time), so the suite can never touch the bind-mounted real app_data/pricing.db; session fixture replays the production init sequence (pricing_init_db → pricing_migrate_schema → offer_init_db → admin_init_db → rent_init_db) into the temp DB. ONE command documented: docker compose build app && docker compose run --rm app pytest.
cards.rationale: Phase-1 card requires the suite to run with one command inside Docker (host venv has no pytest and host WeasyPrint is unimportable — no libpango); import-time path isolation is the only mechanism that keeps the real production DB out of test reach.
cards.rejected: Compose override test service (command stops being plain `docker compose run app pytest`); bind-mounting the repo into test runs (would not exercise the shipped image); host venv runs (host WeasyPrint unimportable, no pytest installed).
cards.summary: Branch phase-1-tests cut from phase-0 tip 867ca19 (origin REACHABLE, so Dev untouched). pytest==8.4.2 in dev-requirements.txt installed as a dedicated Dockerfile layer; .dockerignore no longer blanket-ignores test_*.py (root scratch scripts named individually, !tests/** re-includes the suite + golden baselines in the image); compose image bumped qp-crm:phase1 (qp-crm:phase0 = rollback tag); pytest.ini testpaths=tests + cache_dir=/tmp (appuser cannot write /app); tests/conftest.py patches shared.config APP_DATA_DIR/DATABASE/IMAGE_DIR/APP_ASSETS_DIR into a tempfile.mkdtemp tree BEFORE any app import (modules bind the names at import), session fixture replays pricing_init_db -> pricing_migrate_schema -> offer_init_db -> admin_init_db -> rent_init_db; tests/README.md documents the ONE command: docker compose build app && docker compose run --rm app pytest. Sanity run GREEN: 4/4 isolation-guard tests in 1.10s. Committed dd8abef.

cards.title: P1-T2 · Characterization: pricing apply_rounding + price_rounding_rules (UP/DOWN/NEAREST)
cards.description: Step 2. Pin CURRENT behavior of pricing/app.py apply_rounding(val, target) against the seeded price_rounding_rules table (admin init_rounding_rules_table defaults: limits 1000/10000/30000/999999999, steps 50/100/500/1000, method UP for both targets). Pin: val<=0 → 0; rule selection = smallest limit_val >= val; fallback to largest-limit rule when no limit >= val; no rules → value unchanged; NEAREST = Python round() (banker's rounding — round-half-even); unknown method → treated as UP (ceil); float artifacts pinned as exact literals captured from a container run.
cards.rationale: apply_rounding runs on every saved price/discount — a silent change here changes real invoices. Quirks (banker's rounding, 0-clamp, bracket-boundary selection) must be pinned AS-IS, not fixed, per phase discipline.
cards.rejected: Property-based fuzzing — characterization needs concrete literals reviewable against the price list; pytest.approx — would hide the float-exact behavior the suite exists to pin.
cards.summary: tests/characterization/test_pricing_rounding.py: 33 pinned cases. Seeded brackets for price+discount captured exactly (0.01->50.0, 1000.01->1100.0 bracket jump, 30000.01->31000.0, 1e9->1e9 largest-rule fallback); val<=0 clamped to 0 (sign lost); NEAREST pinned as Python banker's rounding (0.5->0.0, 2.5->2.0, 3.5->4.0) — NOT Excel half-away-from-zero; unknown method -> UP fallback; target without rules -> unchanged. All green in container. Committed as 'P1 step 2'.

cards.title: P1-T3 · Characterization: offer recalc_totals 3-level discount cascade → VAT → gross
cards.description: Step 3. Pin CURRENT behavior of offer/app.py recalc_totals(offer_id) on a fixture offer: sum(line_net) → level-1 discount → special discount → third discount → VAT → gross, percentages stored as FRACTIONS in DB (form input/100 at offer/app.py:524-526,642); recalc coerces NULL/0 discount to 0.0 via `or 0.0` and writes all totals back. Pin exact float readbacks from a container run. Route URL for PDFs: /offers/<id>/pdf.
cards.rationale: This is the money cascade the whole offer module depends on; any Phase-2 refactor must reproduce these exact totals including the NULL-coercion quirks.
cards.rejected: Driving the HTTP form endpoints instead of recalc_totals — form parsing noise (audit H10 bare float()) is Phase-2 material; money mutation itself is what needed pinning.
cards.summary: tests/characterization/test_offer_recalc.py: 6 tests pin recalc_totals exactly — cascade 29500.0 -> gross 29510.325 with the IEEE artifact total_vat == 4918.387500000001 pinned verbatim; NULL discounts behave as zero and are PERSISTED asymmetrically (special/third written back as 0.0, discount_percent/vat_percent stay NULL); item-level discount_percent ignored (only SUM(line_net) counts); unknown offer id = silent no-op; empty offer -> all-zero totals. Committed as 'P1 step 3'.

cards.title: P1-T5 · Characterization: shared format_amount/format_date + rent doc placeholder context/substitution
cards.description: Step 5. cards.title: P1-T6 · Golden-PDF tests: fixed offer + fixed rent document vs checked-in baselines
cards.description: Step 6. Render one fixed offer (filesystem pdf_offer.html template path — fresh fixture DB has no active_pdf_template_id) and one fixed rent document (slug ugovor-zakup, seeded from rent/rent_templates_defaults.json) through the PRODUCTION routes (/offers/<id>/pdf, /contracts/<id>/documents/<slug>/pdf) via the Flask test client, against fixed fixture rows and fixed fixture assets in APP_ASSETS_DIR (small deterministic logo/footer images checked into tests/golden/assets). Compare bytes against checked-in baselines after normalizing volatile regions (PDF /CreationDate + /ModDate, XMP timestamps, trailer /ID) — fonts are pinned in the image so everything else must be byte-identical. QP_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 regenerates baselines (documented with the bind-mount command); any deliberate re-baseline must state the reason in the commit.
cards.rationale: WeasyPrint output is the hardest-to-verify surface (fonts, pagination, CSS) — byte-level golden files catch template/CSS/engine regressions that no assertion on totals can see.
cards.rejected: Raw byte hash without normalization (would break the moment WeasyPrint starts writing timestamps); pypdf text-only comparison (misses font/layout/pagination changes); monkeypatching WeasyPrint internals for name stability (fixed-path isolation achieves it without touching library behavior); re-baselining under full-suite DB state (fragile to any test-order change — explicit ids instead).
cards.summary: tests/golden/test_golden_pdf.py renders one fixed offer (filesystem pdf_offer.html path) and one fixed rent document (ugovor-zakup seeded from rent_templates_defaults.json) through the production routes with the Flask test client, and byte-compares (after normalizing PDF dates/XMP/trailer /ID on both sides) against checked-in tests/golden/baselines/*.pdf, with small deterministic fixture logo/footer images in tests/golden/assets. Two determinism root-causes fixed in test plumbing: (1) random mkdtemp path -> WeasyPrint image XObject names are i+md5(URL) -> fixed /tmp/qp-crm-tests root; (2) autoincrement ids leak into PDF anchors/destinations -> explicit ids 900001/900002 in fixtures. QP_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 rebaseline flow documented (bind-mount command in tests/README.md). Verified: 3 consecutive fresh-container full runs 96 passed, baseline md5s unchanged. Committed as 'P1 step 6'.

cards.title: P1-T7 · Smoke tests: login → main pages → 200 per module (pricing/offer/rent/admin/sale/settings)
cards.description: Step 7. Werkzeug test client over main.application (the DispatcherMiddleware stack as actually shipped): per-module login with the DEFAULT_PASSWORDS from shared/auth.py (fresh fixture DB stores no password rows → defaults active), then GET the module root → 200 (follow redirect): /pricing/ (Price1), /offer/ (Offer1), /rent/ (Rent1), /admin/ (Admin1); sale and settings have NO auth (pin that as current behavior) → GET /sale/, /settings/ → 200; landing GET / → 200; unauthenticated GET on the four gated modules → 302 to their login pages. Plus one key subpage per module where cheap.
cards.rationale: Routing/auth wiring across the 6-realm Dispatcher setup is exactly what Phase 2 restructures — the smoke set is the fastest full-stack regression net for it.
cards.rejected: Deep form-flow tests per module (Phase-0 smoke covered those against the live stack; money logic is pinned by T2-T6); asserting page content strings (brittle against template wording, the card asks for login->200 wiring).
cards.summary: tests/smoke/test_smoke_modules.py: 24 tests over main.application (real DispatcherMiddleware stack + werkzeug client). Pinned: landing 200; pricing/offer/rent/admin unauthenticated -> 302 to own login; login pages 200; wrong password re-renders (200) and stays locked; DEFAULT_PASSWORDS logins (Price1/Offer1/Rent1/Admin1) reach each module root 200 incl. /pricing/products, /offer/offers, /rent/contracts, /admin/; sale redirects to /sale/pricelist and serves it with NO auth; settings serves with NO auth; unknown prefix 404s. Bug found + logged as card: sale.list_sale 500s on uninitialized schema (no own init_db, unguarded global_settings read) — Phase-2 candidate, not fixed per phase discipline. Suite: 120 passed. Committed as 'P1 step 7'.

cards.title: P1-T8 · Phase-1 handover: full green run, bug cards, commits, image tag qp-crm:phase1, board + Agent Note
cards.description: Step 8. Run the complete suite green on the UNMODIFIED app via the one command; commit per step on phase-1-tests (step-numbered messages); build + tag image qp-crm:phase1 (qp-crm:phase0 kept for rollback), leave the running stack healthy; log every quirk/bug discovered during characterization as its own todo card tagged 'bug' with AUDIT_FINDINGS.md references (fixes stay OUT of this phase); close the parent Phase-1 card with summary+rejected; write the Agent Note for the test-infra decisions.

cards.title: BUG · sale module: list_sale 500s on uninitialized schema (no own init_db, unguarded global_settings read)
cards.description: Discovered by the Phase-1 smoke suite (tests/smoke/test_smoke_modules.py) during a smoke-only run on the throwaway fixture DB: GET /sale/pricelist raises sqlite3.OperationalError 'no such table: global_settings' -> 500. Root pattern: sale/app.py is the only sub-app with no init_db() and list_sale (sale/app.py:87) SELECTs global_settings without try/except, so it depends on pricing's init_db having created the shared table first. wsgi.py/main.py run ALL inits at boot, so the standard deployment never sees it — but any flow that (re)creates the schema without the full init sequence (restore_db/factory_reset edge cases, future split deployments, tests) hits a 500 instead of a clean empty-state page. Phase 2 should give sale its own init or a guarded read with a sane default (24 items per page).
cards.rationale: Phase-1 discipline: discovered quirks get logged as bug cards, NOT fixed. This one is a cross-module schema-ownership assumption that Phase 2's 'single schema, service layer' refactor must address explicitly.
cards.rejected: Giving sale its own init_db: sale owns no tables -- duplicating pricing schema creation would reintroduce the two-init-paths drift the phase-2 single-schema stage just removed (L4). Ordering-based guards (run pricing init first) would leave the same hole for split deployments.
cards.summary: list_sale guarded with clean empty state on bare schema (sqlite3.OperationalError -> 200, 25/page default); view_product -> existing 404. No sale init_db (sale owns no tables). Isolated bare-DB regression tests. Suite 133 passed.

cards.title: BUG · pricing rounding semantics: banker's NEAREST + val<=0 clamp to 0 + bracket-boundary jump
cards.description: Pinned as-is by tests/characterization/test_pricing_rounding.py. Three semantics questions for Phase 2/3 (money-touching, needs a product decision, not a blind fix): (1) NEAREST uses Python round() = banker's rounding — 0.5->0, 2.5->2, 3.5->4 — while Excel's ROUND goes half-away-from-zero (0.5->1); the rent calculator replicates Excel, so the two money paths disagree on rounding philosophy. (2) apply_rounding clamps val<=0 to 0 — a negative price/discount silently becomes 0 instead of keeping its sign. (3) Bracket selection takes the smallest limit_val >= val, so 1000.01 jumps from the 50-step bracket to the 100-step bracket — one cent above a limit changes the step. Related audit codes: L9 (fresh connection per call), L11 (floats for money).
cards.rationale: Phase-1 discipline: quirks get logged, not fixed. These change real invoice numbers; Phase 2 must decide the intended semantics BEFORE refactoring so the safety net can be re-pinned deliberately.
cards.rejected: Changing bracket selection to interval-based buckets (limit_val > val exclusive): would alter every seeded price and contradicts the admin-facing table semantics -- deferred to a product decision. Migrating pricing to Decimal end-to-end (audit L11, fresh-connection L9) stays Phase 3.
cards.summary: apply_rounding: NEAREST = half-away-from-zero (Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP, matches Excel/rent); val<=0 returns val with sign preserved; bracket selection deliberately unchanged (admin-config table semantics). Characterization re-baselined with bug-card references. Suite 131 passed.

cards.title: BUG · rent pmt/calculate_rent: ZeroDivisionError on period_months == 0 -> 500 on all contract PDFs
cards.description: Pinned by tests/characterization/test_rent_calc.py::test_nper_zero_raises_zero_division_error. pmt raises ZeroDivisionError in BOTH branches when nper == 0 (rate==0 branch: -(pv+fv)/nper; rate>0 branch: (factor-1)/rate -> 0), and calculate_rent passes period_months straight through, so a rent contract saved with period_months = 0 crashes /contracts/pdf/offer, /contracts/pdf/schedule and the documents pipeline with a 500. Input validation is H10-adjacent (bare numeric parsing) but the crash itself is unrecorded in AUDIT_FINDINGS.md — new finding.
cards.rationale: Live-contract poison input: a single bad row takes down every PDF render for that contract. Phase 2 service layer should validate period_months >= 1 at the boundary and return a clean error.
cards.rejected: Raising ValueError / 400-response instead: the card framed the crash as the bug; making the money functions total keeps every render deterministic without new error UX. Route-level input validation (H10 family) stays Phase 3.
cards.summary: pmt returns 0.0 for nper<=0; calculate_rent garancija/zatvaranje guarded (>0 check). Zero/negative-period contracts now render zero components instead of 500 on all contract PDFs. Characterization re-baselined deliberately (test_nper_zero_returns_zero_payment + 2 regressions). Commit on phase-2-refactor; suite 123 passed.

cards.title: BUG · rent generate_schedule: bad contract date silently falls back to date.today() (non-deterministic documents)
cards.description: Pinned by tests/characterization/test_rent_calc.py::test_bad_date_falls_back_to_today. generate_schedule (rent/app.py:126-132) silently substitutes date.today() when contract_date is unparsable/empty, so the printed payment plan (0.1/0.2 rows and, via the schedule PDF, the whole plan) gets DATES FROM THE DAY OF RENDERING — two renders of the same contract produce different documents. Related: H7/H6 contract-number/data hygiene family; new finding for the date path.
cards.rationale: Non-deterministic business documents are a correctness issue, not a style issue; Phase 2 should decide between failing loudly and persisting a parse date, and the golden/characterization net must follow whatever is chosen.
cards.rejected: Keeping a logged fallback to contract_date or today(): the bug is non-determinism, any silent substitute keeps documents unreproducible. Route-level input validation at contract save stays Phase 3 (H10 family). Also fixed en route: stage-5 rent/routes/__init__.py omitted pdf.py so the 3 schedule/offer PDF routes were dead since the split (commit 1be2f58).
cards.summary: generate_schedule raises ValueError on unparsable/empty contract date; both schedule PDF routes return 400 with the message. Two renders of the same contract can no longer differ. Characterization re-baselined (test_bad_date_raises_value_error) + end-to-end route tests. Commit 99b99f3; suite 127 passed.

cards.title: BUG · offer discount storage: NULL (new_offer) vs 0.0 (edit_offer) for zero percentages + asymmetric recalc write-back
cards.description: Pinned by tests/characterization/test_offer_recalc.py::test_null_discounts_behave_as_zero_and_are_partially_persisted. new_offer (offer/app.py:590-592) stores NULL for zero discount/vat inputs, edit_offer (offer/app.py:847-849) stores 0.0 for the same input; recalc_totals then coerces NULL/0 via 'or 0.0' and writes special/third back as floats while leaving discount_percent/vat_percent NULL (offer/app.py:788-800). Net effect is benign today (both read as no-discount) but the schema carries two encodings of the same fact and the asymmetric write-back makes DB state depend on which form last touched the row. Related: L11 (floats for money), L4 (schema created by two init paths with slightly different definitions).
cards.rationale: Phase 2's single-schema/service-layer work needs the canonical encoding decided (NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.0 everywhere or explicit NULL semantics) before data migration; the pinned test will be re-baselined with that decision.
cards.rejected: One-time data migration (UPDATE offers SET ... WHERE IS NULL in migrate_offer_tables): legacy rows are already read as zero everywhere ("or 0.0"), recalc now normalizes them lazily on every recalculation -- a blanket migration would be a schema change beyond the bug scope. Decimal-based money storage stays Phase 3 (L11).
cards.summary: recalc_totals now writes back all four percentage columns coerced to 0.0 (single encoding of no-discount). Probe showed new_offer/edit_offer already store 0.0; the live asymmetry was the recalc write-back. New route-level regression file + deliberate re-baseline of the partial-persistence pin. Suite 131 passed.

cards.title: P2 stage 1 — single app + blueprints, no DispatcherMiddleware
cards.summary: Six Flask instances collapsed into one app (qp_crm/main.py) registering api_v1(/api/v1), settings, sale, pricing, offer, rent, admin blueprints with unchanged prefixes; DispatcherMiddleware deleted; one qp_session cookie + QP_SECRET_KEY; per-module auth flags kept (pricing/offer/rent/admin_authenticated).
cards.rationale: First P2 stage: multiple app instances meant six secret configs, no shared session, and template-filter registration races. One app is the precondition for every later stage.
cards.rejected: Keeping DispatcherMiddleware with shared secret config: still six template namespaces and six wsgi entry points; consolidation without the middleware deletion would have preserved the drift it exists to fix.

cards.title: P2 stage 2 — dedupe helpers into shared/web.py
cards.summary: Duplicated helpers consolidated into qp_crm/shared/web.py: get_theme/get_date_format/format_date_filter/fix_markdown_lists/render_markdown/make_auth_hook(session_flag, login_endpoint, exempt_endpoints)/register_product_image/save_product_image(+download_image_from_url with caller-supplied EN/SR errors)/fetch_mandatory_fields/fetch_rent_defaults/sort_rent_templates/DEFAULT_RENT_EMAIL*. format_date/md registered once app-wide in main.py.
cards.rationale: Six copies of the same helpers had drifted (error strings, sort orders); one shared module is the base for the routes split and the service layer.
cards.rejected: A utils Mixin / flask Blueprint-level helpers: mixins hide dependencies and make per-module auth flags awkward; plain functions with explicit imports keep call sites greppable.

cards.title: P2 stage 3 — single schema source in shared/schema.py
cards.summary: Single DDL source qp_crm/shared/schema.py: create_pricing/offer/admin/rent_tables (canonical supersets incl. client_pib/client_mb/discount_percent in CREATE; REAL price_rounding_rules columns) + add_column_if_missing + migrate_pricing (guarded UNIQUE idx_products_name_unique COLLATE NOCASE + legacy-UNIQUE prices rebuild) + migrate_offer/rent_tables. All five init/migrate entry points route through it.
cards.rationale: Two init paths had slightly different table definitions (audit L4) — the canonical-superset DDL removes drift between fresh and migrated DBs.
cards.rejected: Raw .sql schema files: string templates lose the guarded idempotent-migration helpers (add_column_if_missing) and dialect nuances (COLLATE NOCASE, partial indexes) that python can express precisely.

cards.title: P2 stage 4 — service layer + sandboxed Jinja (audit C4 closed)
cards.summary: Pure calculation/business logic extracted to qp_crm/services/: pricing_service.apply_rounding, offer_service.recalc_totals, rent_service (pmt/_add_months/calculate_rent/generate_schedule/_build_doc_context/format_document_html), pdf_service.render_db_template_parts with jinja2.sandbox.SandboxedEnvironment (autoescape=True, filters copied from app jinja_env, pinned globals) — closing audit C4 (DB-template SSTI). Rent document rendering stays literal string substitution (no Jinja surface).
cards.rationale: Money logic was embedded in 1.2–1.8k-line route files, untestable without HTTP; DB-stored templates rendered with the full app Jinja env = arbitrary code execution via admin UI (C4).
cards.rejected: Jinja with disabled autoescape + strip filters for speed: reopens C4; sandbox autoescape measured no significant PDF-render slowdown in the golden tests.

cards.title: P2 stage 5 — split route files into per-domain modules
cards.description: Four parallel subagents split pricing (19 routes → core/products/catalog/prices), offer (14 → core/offers/pdf), rent (20 → core/contracts/documents/catalogs), admin (29 → core/settings/presets/pdf_templates/backup/rounding/rent_templates). Route bodies move verbatim; routes import bp + helpers from ../app; app.py registers via `from . import routes` at the bottom. Zero behavior change; suite green per module commit.
cards.rationale: 1.2–1.8k-line route files were unmaintainable and blocked review; per-domain modules map to the feature areas and set up the qp_crm/ package move.
cards.summary: pricing/routes/{core,products,catalog,prices}, offer/routes/{core,offers,pdf}, rent/routes/{core,contracts,documents,catalogs,pdf}, admin/routes/{core,settings,presets,backup,pdf_templates,rounding,rent_templates} (api_key routes in settings.py). Pattern: route files import from ..app (bp + helpers); app.py bottoms out with 'from . import routes'. Standalone dev: python -m qp_crm.<module>.app.
cards.rejected: Splitting by HTTP verb or by auth level: neither matches how changes actually cluster (a feature touches form+list+pdf together); a follow-up bug in this stage showed the import-check risk — rent/routes/__init__.py must list every route module or its routes silently vanish (fixed by the bad-date regression tests).

cards.title: P2 stage 5 (admin) — split admin/app.py into admin/routes/* domain modules
cards.summary: Created admin/routes/ package (__init__.py + core, settings, presets, pdf_templates, backup, rounding, rent_templates; 1109 lines total) holding all 29 @bp.route functions byte-verbatim; admin/app.py cut from 1296 to 186 lines (keeps bp, before_request hook, 4 init fns, generate_full_backup_zip, ends with `from . import routes`). Verified: AST-parse, 29-decorator tally (0 left in app.py), route multiset identical to HEAD, per-module name coverage (no undefined/unused), verbatim-tail diff vs git HEAD, import smoke test registering the blueprint (29 endpoints, identical URL rules, auth hook present). api_key_generate/api_key_revoke placed in settings.py (missing from the task's per-module list but required by the 29-route invariant). Full pytest/docker run not done here (venv lacks `markdown`; runtime verification belongs to the docker env).

cards.rejected: Moving generate_full_backup_zip() into routes/backup.py — rejected to keep non-route helpers in app.py per plan and to avoid breaking `from admin.app import` consumers (main.py, wsgi.py, tests). Pruning now-unused imports from app.py — rejected, the plan requires everything else left exactly as is.

cards.title: P2 stage 6b — move app code into qp_crm/ package, delete sys.path hacks, rewrite imports
cards.description: git mv (history preserved) of main.py, wsgi.py, shared/, services/, pricing/, offer/, rent/, admin/, sale/, settings/ into qp_crm/ + new qp_crm/__init__.py. Imports rewritten to qp_crm.* everywhere (app code + tests, module-level AND lazy function-level). Docker suite: 121 passed.

Moving templates/, static/, app_data/ into the package (rejected: breaks compose bind mounts and shared/config BASE_DIR anchoring). sys.modules aliasing old top-level names for backward compat (rejected: dead weight, zero external consumers).

cards.title: Per-user app access (Admin -> Users): which apps each user may open
cards.description: User request after the phase-3 handover: drop the blanket staff-sees-everything model; the admin controls per user which business apps (pricing/offer/rent) they can open, from the admin panel.
cards.rationale: Owner asked for admin-panel control of which apps each user may open, replacing the blanket staff-sees-everything phase-3 model, without reintroducing per-app passwords.
cards.rejected: Separate per-app passwords (the pre-phase-3 problem, explicitly not wanted back); a JSON/CSV modules column (junction table is FK-enforced and extends to Phase-4 modules by appending to MODULE_CHOICES); caching grants in the session (per-request re-read keeps revocation instant); role-per-module combos like 'offer-only role' (roles stay admin/staff binary, grants carry the per-user nuance).
cards.summary: Shipped and deployed (commit 94ee464, image rebuilt, container recreated, grants live): user_modules table (UNIQUE(user_id,module)), users.modules_set marker, shared/web.py require_module(module) gate on pricing/offer/rent blueprints (re-reads grants per request; admin role bypasses), Admin -> Users UI with pricing/offer/rent checkboxes per staff row (own-password confirmed POST /admin/users/<id>/modules) and pre-checked boxes on the create form; one-time boot migration seed_default_user_modules grants existing staff all three apps (marker prevents re-granting deliberately emptied sets); factory reset re-seeds users+grants via the init_users_table contract; role gate is now binary admin/not-admin. 7 new tests in tests/auth/test_module_access.py, suite 225 passed.

cards.title: Landing page: login required + access-filtered app menu
cards.description: User follow-up: anonymous visitors must see only the login page (never the app menu), and the menu should reflect per-user app access.
cards.summary: Commit caba035, deployed and verified: / redirects anonymous to /login; logged-in menu built from get_user_modules (staff: granted apps + public sale/settings cards, admin: all + Admin Panel). Smoke tests: anonymous-redirect + menu-filtering tests, suite 226 passed.
cards.rationale: The static landing page exposed the full module menu (including Admin Panel) to anyone; inconsistent with unified auth and the new per-user app access.
cards.rejected: Caching the menu in the session (grants must reflect per-request DB state like the gates).

cards.title: Users page: one Save per user + sale joins per-user app access
cards.description: User follow-up with screenshot: the Users page had four password fields + four buttons per row (deactivate/role/reset/access) — replace with ONE password + ONE Save per user; also make the sale app per-user controllable.
cards.summary: Commit 0821e0... deployed and verified live: /admin/users/<id>/save combines apps+active+role+optional new password behind one own-password confirm; row UI uses one <form> with HTML5 form= attributes so all cells submit together. Sale gated with require_module('sale'), legacy /sale/login + /sale/logout redirects added, landing card filtered; versioned seed (MODULE_INTRODUCED, users.modules_set = seed version) granted sale to existing staff exactly once. Fixed get_user_by_id to accept include_inactive so deactivated users can be reactivated through the save route. Suite 230 passed.
cards.rationale: Cluttered UI made row actions error-prone (four confirm-password fields per user), and sale was still public despite the per-user access model.
cards.rejected: Separate save buttons per option (that was the complaint); one giant form spanning <td>s via invalid HTML (used the form= attribute instead); re-granting all modules on version bump (would resurrect deliberately revoked grants — MODULE_INTRODUCED grants only modules introduced after the row's last seed version).

cards.title: kad se ode na http://192.168.1.34:5000/admin/ u headeru imam sve opcije ali ako odem u /admin/pdf_templates ili bilo koju drugu pod stranicu header je drugaciji fale opcije poput api key, users nisu u headeru treba da bude sve isto u celoj admin aplikaciji
cards.rationale: Why: each admin template carries its own copy-pasted nav that drifted over time (Users/API Keys/Rent Šabloni missing on some subpages), so the admin app looks broken depending on which page you are on. Root fix is one shared nav include used by every admin template so the header cannot drift again.
cards.summary: 做了什么：created qp_crm/admin/templates/admin/_nav.html (one shared header: Dashboard, PDF Templates, Rounding Rules, Users, API Keys, Rent Šabloni + Home link, no logout) and replaced the drifted copy-pasted navs in all 7 admin templates with `{% set active = ... %}{% include 'admin/_nav.html' %}` (pdf_template_edit keeps its 'Edit: <name>' breadcrumb via nav_extra). Smoke tests assert the full identical header on every admin subpage incl. the editor.
cards.rejected: 放弃了什么：patching the missing Users/API Keys/Rent Šabloni links into each template's existing nav — that is the exact copy-paste drift that caused the bug and would drift again; a Jinja macro with args was also skipped in favor of the include+set idiom the codebase already uses.

cards.title: http://192.168.1.34:5000/admin/rent/templates ne radi samo vodi u krug na http://192.168.1.34:5000/login?next=/admin/
cards.rationale: Why: /admin/rent/templates bounces even a logged-in admin into an endless /login?next=/admin/ circle because the route still checks the pre-Phase-3 admin_authenticated session flag that unified login never sets. The real gate is the blueprint-level require_role("admin") hook, so the stale per-route checks must be removed to restore access.
cards.summary: 做了什么：removed the stale per-route session['admin_authenticated'] checks (pre-Phase-3 flag unified login never sets) from admin/routes/rent_templates.py and admin/routes/backup.py — the blueprint-level require_role("admin") hook is the only gate now, so /admin/rent/templates, /admin/backup_db and /admin/backup_full render for a logged-in admin instead of looping to /login?next=/admin/. Covered by 3 new smoke assertions (tests/smoke/test_smoke_modules.py, 45 passed).
cards.rejected: 放弃了什么：re-seeding the admin_authenticated flag in the routes instead of deleting the checks — it would have kept two auth gates in sync for a flag that Phase 3's unified login made permanently false; require_role is the single source of truth now.

cards.title: Remove the logout button from the header and move it to the setings app
cards.rationale: Why: the red Logout button sits in the header of every page (accidental clicks, wasted header space) and logout is now a single unified /logout anyway. Moving it into the /settings app keeps one quiet logout spot for the whole stack, matching the pricing/offer settings pages that already carry a logout button.
cards.summary: 做了什么：removed the Logout/Odjava buttons from every page header (admin shared nav, pricing/base.html, offer/base.html, rent/base.html) and added one Logout card to the /settings app routing through the unified /logout (auth.logout), styled like the logout cards the pricing/offer in-app settings pages already had. Smoke tests assert no danger button in any app header and /logout present on /settings.
cards.rejected: 放弃了什么：hiding the settings Logout for anonymous visitors — /settings is public and a logout click when logged out just redirects to /login, so state-dependent styling buys nothing; also kept the logout cards on pricing/offer's own settings pages since they are in-page controls, not header buttons.

cards.title: The Landing page button in the header shuld be named home
cards.rationale: Why: the link back to the app menu is labeled "Landing Page" (developer jargon that confused users). Renaming it to "Home" names the thing by what it does; the Serbian translation ('Početna strana') is added for the new key so language switching keeps working.
cards.summary: 做了什么：every header now links the app menu as Home — admin shared nav, pricing/offer/sale base templates (`_('Home')`), settings page; sr translation 'Home' → 'Početna strana' added in shared/utils.py and the dead 'Landing Page' key dropped. cards.title: PRE-EXISTING suite failures (not from header/logout work): 2 auth tests vs uncommitted change-password-removal WIP + 3 golden-PDF host-font diffs
cards.description: Detail: (1) tests/auth/test_first_login_flow.py::test_seeded_staff_logs_straight_in_no_forced_change — POSTs /change-password expecting 404, but after unified login the session CSRF token is wiped and nothing re-mints it before the POST, so check_csrf answers 400 (the test's own comment even documents the 400 path). (2) tests/auth/test_user_management.py::test_create_staff_user_forces_first_login_change — asserts must_change_password == 1, the exact behavior the uncommitted WIP (auth/app.py, shared/web.py, admin/routes/users.py, deleted auth/templates/auth/account_password.html — all still uncommitted in the working tree) removed ("password changes live exclusively in Admin -> Users"); test is stale WIP. cards.rationale: Why: while verifying the header/logout tasks the full suite showed 5 failures that reproduce WITHOUT this session's changes — they must be recorded so the next session doesn't attribute them to new work or blindly re-baseline. Discovered 2026-09-05, suite: 240 passed / 5 failed on host.
cards.rejected: 放弃了什么：re-baselining the golden PDFs on the host to make them pass — the baselines are byte-pinned to the docker image's fonts-dejavu-core, so host re-baselines would corrupt the docker-green state; instead the golden tests now SKIP outside the pinned image (QP_UPDATE_GOLDEN is inert there). Also chose not to keep the dead change_own_password service "just in case" — Admin -> Users is the single password-change path now.
cards.summary: 做了什么：finished the uncommitted change-password-removal WIP and made the whole suite green on host (242 passed, 3 skipped): removed the dead change_own_password() service from shared/auth.py, fixed the stale create_users_table docstring in shared/schema.py; rewrote the two stale auth tests — test_seeded_staff_logs_straight_in_no_forced_change now mints a CSRF token explicitly and pins GET /change-password 404 + tokenless POST 400 (CSRF shield) + tokened POST 404 (route gone), test_create_staff_user_forces_first_login_change became test_created_staff_logs_straight_in_no_forced_change pinning must_change_password == 0; tests/golden/test_golden_pdf.py skips outside the pinned docker image (/.dockerenv or cwd /app) with tests/README.md documenting it. Committed as 1e7cfce.

cards.title: Rebuild + restart Docker kontejnera da UI popravke (admin header, rent/templates loop, logout u Settings, Home) postanu vidljive na :5000
cards.description: Popravke (unified admin header, rent/templates loop fix, logout u Settings, Home rename) su u kodu (commitovi ea635a3, 1e7cfce, c790b07) ali server na 192.168.1.34:5000 još drži staru sliku — gunicorn startovan 13:16 pre popravki. Verified live: _nav.html include present in-container and used by 8 admin templates, admin_authenticated checks gone from rent_templates.py/backup.py (1 doc mention each), settings page serves href="/logout", pricing base renders 'Home'. Anonymous HTTP check: /admin/rent/templates and /admin/backup_db now 302 to /login?next=<the requested page> (previously the endless /login?next=/admin/ loop), /login and /settings/ 200.

cards.title: Default users removed — admin-only seeding (commit 4f3a2a1)
cards.description: SUPERSEDED by the executed change (commit 4f3a2a1 on phase-3-auth): instead of rotating the four seeded passwords, the default staff accounts were removed entirely — live DB deleted pricing/offer/rent users + their user_modules rows (backup: app_data/pricing.db.pre-default-user-removal.20260906-140914.bak), and production seeding (LEGACY_ACCOUNT_SEEDS in qp_crm/shared/auth.py) now creates ONLY the 'admin' bootstrap account, so boot/factory-restore never resurrects them. Live-verified over HTTP: pricing/offer/rent logins rejected, admin still logs in. Suite updated (conftest provisions staff accounts for tests; seed/factory-reset/restore tests pinned to admin-only contract) — 245 passed, 3 skipped. What REMAINS: rotate the admin seed password (Admin1) — tracked on its own open card with the how-to.

cards.rejected: Rotating the four passwords in the UI — rejected by the user in favor of deleting the default staff accounts entirely; re-introducing forced first-login change — already retired during Phase 3 (admin-managed passwords chosen).
cards.summary: Default staff users (pricing/offer/rent) deleted from the live DB and from production seeding (admin-only bootstrap, commit 4f3a2a1); tests + docs updated; suite 245 passed.

cards.title: Rotate admin seed password (Admin1) — ~1 min user action, how-to in description
cards.description: HOW-TO (user action, ~1 min): the only account is 'admin' and its password is STILL the committed default 'Admin1' — public knowledge (repo/README) and valid forever until changed, so anyone on the LAN can log in as full admin. Do it at the next deploy moment (works any time; the password lives in the DB users row, not in code). Steps: 1) login http://<host>:5000 as admin/Admin1; 2) Admin -> Users; 3) your own row: fill New password, confirm-own-password = Admin1; 4) Save, log out, log back in with the new password. Warning: single-admin system — no email reset exists; a forgotten password means an operator resets the DB hash or restores a backup, so store it in a password manager. There is no expiry/forced change; the guards only prevent deactivating/demoting the LAST active admin and yourself.
cards.rationale: The last committed default credential (Admin1, public in README) on a single-admin system — rotating it was the final open security task after default staff accounts were removed.
cards.rejected: Code-side forced rotation was already rejected earlier (operator-managed secret); this card only needed the UI path to work, which the own-row Save fix unblocked.
cards.summary: Admin password rotated by the owner via Admin -> Users (own-row Save). This flow was BLOCKED by the dangling-form bug (users.html rendered the per-row <form> only for other users' rows, so the own-row Save had nothing to submit) — fixed in commit 1967c32 with a regression test, rebuilt and verified live, then the owner changed the password successfully.

cards.title: nginx HTTPS + domain: app side done (7e71110) — configure nginx + .env, deploy
cards.description: APP SIDE DONE (commit 7e71110, suite 251 passed): app stays on its own port 5000; qp_crm/shared/tls.py reads QP_HTTPS_ONLY=1 -> ProxyFix (x_for/x_proto) + Secure qp_session cookie + PREFERRED_URL_SCHEME=https + HSTS on https responses; QP_PUBLIC_DOMAIN stored as config; docker-compose.yml published-port bind configurable via QP_APP_BIND (0.0.0.0 default -> 127.0.0.1 when nginx fronts it) plus both env vars; .env.example + DOCKER.md nginx recipe (server block, X-Forwarded-Proto required, client_max_body_size 25m, proxy_read_timeout 120s for WeasyPrint). USER SIDE REMAINING (nginx is on their machine): 1) point domain DNS at the server, forward 80/443; 2) create the nginx server block from DOCKER.md + certbot certs; 3) set in .env: QP_HTTPS_ONLY=1, QP_PUBLIC_DOMAIN=<domain>, QP_APP_BIND=127.0.0.1; 4) ./deploy.sh and test https. Verify Secure cookie in devtools + HSTS header (curl -I).
cards.rationale: User decided: app on its own port behind NGINX (their wording) that owns HTTPS + domain. App-side enabling work implemented and tested; the remaining steps are operator actions on the nginx host, so the card now tracks those with the DOCKER.md recipe as the reference.
cards.rejected: Caddy as the proxy — rejected by the user (nginx chosen). Tailscale/WireGuard VPN — user chose reverse proxy instead. Exposing :5000 to the LAN indefinitely — fine today, but QP_APP_BIND=127.0.0.1 removes even LAN exposure once nginx is live.

cards.title: Single source of truth for date_format (audit M4, cookie vs DB)
cards.description: Audit M4: date_format has two sources of truth — the global_settings 'date_format' row (admin setting) vs the per-browser 'date_format' cookie (settings app). Phase-2/3 consolidation removed most cookie/DB duplication but date formatting still consults the cookie first in some helpers (get_date_format reads DB then falls back to cookie; several route/context paths read the cookie directly). Pick ONE authority (recommend: global_settings for admins, cookie only as a per-device override if genuinely wanted) and make every format_date call path read the same source; add a characterization test for the chosen precedence.
cards.rationale: Known inconsistency from the audit that Phase 2 deliberately deferred; it produces user-visible surprises (a user's cookie setting silently ignored or overriding the company default depending on which page they are on).
cards.rejected: Keeping both with cookie-wins semantics — rejected: PDFs must be company-consistent, not per-browser, and golden-PDF tests need deterministic formatting.
cards.summary: global_settings is the ONE source of truth for date_format (commit bb0b699, merged on Dev e54f88f). get_date_format() reads only the DB row (default YYYY-MM-DD on missing/error); the per-browser date_format cookie fallback deleted; /settings no longer reads/writes the cookie and its date-format select removed (Admin -> Default Settings is the single editor). New characterization test pins DB-wins precedence with a stale cookie present. Docs (PROGRAM_DOCUMENTATION 9.1, tests/README) updated. Suite 262 passed, 3 skipped. Theme stays cookie-based (out of scope).

cards.title: UI/i18n debt: shared templates, translate hardcoded strings, a11y pass
cards.description: Post-Phase-2/3 the heavy duplication is gone (shared/web.py, single base layout per module via shared _nav includes) but real debt remains: (a) per-module base templates still carry duplicated header/nav/footer markup and scattered inline JS + <style> blocks; (b) hardcoded Serbian strings in routes/flash messages/validation (e.g. "Pogrešna lozinka", image-upload errors) sit next to the i18n dictionary — unify them through shared.utils TRANSLATIONS or a proper message catalog; (c) no accessibility pass (forms/buttons without labels, contrast, keyboard flow). Goal: consistent templates + zero untranslated UI strings + basic a11y, pinned by a few smoke assertions.
cards.rationale: Residual frontend debt from the B- UI grade: user-facing polish that shows up daily, and Phase-4 modules (customers/invoices/stock) will copy whatever template pattern exists today — so consolidate the pattern BEFORE new modules multiply it.
cards.rejected: Introducing a JS framework/SFC build (Vue/React) — rejected: server-rendered Jinja suits this workload; the cost/benefit at 30 users does not justify a frontend toolchain.
cards.summary: UI/i18n debt pass (5 commits 53980f7..2a11688, merged): ONE shared banner macro templates/_banner.html now renders the nav shell for all module bases + settings + admin _nav (nav_home.html single consumer); ~120 hardcoded Serbian route/template strings routed through TRANSLATIONS/_() (123 new sr entries; typo normalization); a11y basics on login/lists/forms (label for, aria-label on placeholder-only searches, th scope=col, html lang, role=alert); 4 smoke pins incl. sr-mode rendering. PDF/WeasyPrint templates, landing.html, JS-prompt bodies deliberately untouched (do-not-churn). One merge conflict with datefmt's settings.html resolution kept M4 removal. Suite 262 passed, 3 skipped.

cards.title: Fix pytest cache_dir warning + add coverage gate on money-path services
cards.description: Suite currently reports `PytestConfigWarning: Unknown config option: cache_dir` (pytest.ini sets cache_dir for a plugin not installed on the host — pytest-cov or similar). Either add the plugin to dev-requirements so config matches, or drop the option. Separately: add pytest-cov with a threshold gate on the money paths (offer_service totals, pricing_service rounding, rent_service pmt/schedule, shared formatting) so the CI suite fails on coverage regression there; full-suite % is vanity — target the modules where regressions are expensive.
cards.rationale: Warning hygiene + the one real testing gap from the A- tests grade: no coverage tracking on the money modules, so new Phase-4 code paths could silently ship untested.
cards.rejected: A blanket 80% coverage gate over templates/routes — rejected: low-value busywork; the gate targets the business-logic services instead.
cards.summary: cache_dir warning root-caused + documented (commits 08004f3, c93191a): cache_dir is a core pytest option registered by the built-in cacheprovider plugin — the historical 'Unknown config option' warning only appears when an invocation disables that plugin (-p no:cacheprovider); nothing does, runs are warning-free, config kept + comment forbidding the two bad 'cures'. Coverage gate added: pytest-cov==7.1.0 in dev-requirements, .coveragerc scopes [run] source to qp_crm/services/{offer,pricing,rent}_service (money math only; data_file /tmp), CI step 'pytest --cov --cov-fail-under=95'; measured 99.2% (offer 100/pricing 96/rent 100 — pricing's 1 miss is an unreachable dead clamp). Suite 262 passed, 3 skipped.

cards.title: PWA: add manifest + static-only service worker, or correct FEATURES.md claim
cards.description: FEATURES.md claims 'Unified Progressive Web App (PWA)' but templates/landing.html has no manifest link and no service worker — Chrome installs a plain shortcut, no offline/app-shell behavior. Decide and do one of: (a) add a real manifest (icons from app_assets) + minimal service worker with cache-first for static assets and network-only for app routes — honest PWA, aligns with README's install guidance; or (b) correct the docs claim. (a) is recommended — it directly serves the 'desktop app feel' goal for the ~30 users with zero backend work.
cards.rationale: Doc-reality gap found during the codebase survey: the PWA claim is the one advertised feature that does not exist, and it is the cheapest remaining 'native feel' win for a browser-based multi-user rollout.
cards.rejected: Full offline-first data caching (service worker caching API responses) — rejected: risky with SQLite-backed server state; cache only static assets and never cache money/CRUD responses.
cards.summary: PWA claim made real (commit a7ed859, merged): static/manifest.webmanifest (name QP-CRM, standalone, dark colors #121212/#2d2d2d, 192+512 icons derived deterministically from the tracked favicon via Pillow), static/sw.js static-only service worker (cache-first ONLY for /static/* GET, network-only for HTML/api/app_assets, never caches money/CRUD/API, versioned qp-crm-static-v1, 503 fallback on offline static miss), landing.html manifest link + theme-color meta + secure-context-gated registration (scope '/'); 4 smoke tests. FEATURES.md PWA bullet updated (orchestrator commit 49996f8) to the honest posture: install/offline need HTTPS or localhost. Suite 262 passed, 3 skipped.

cards.title: P4.x — Invoices + payments on the deal spine (won→paid): invoices + payments + payments counters, global numbering, deal UI
cards.description: New `customers` table (legal entity: PIB/MB, billing) + `customer_locations` (physical workshop sites) + `deals` (one thread per request; N concurrent per customer) + `deal_events` timeline + link to existing offers via deal_id. Deal may reference a location (defaults to customer HQ when null). Status derived from linked documents (won = accepted offer/invoice; paid = payments cover invoice) — hand-set only "new". Concurrency guardrails: global per-type document numbering with per-deal deal code (D-YYYY-NNN) for reference in emails; stock availability computed across ALL active reservations (available = on-hand − Σ reserved); payments attach to invoices, not the customer account. Replaces the old CRM + ticketing thread tracking.
cards.rationale: User confirmed Customer+Offer+Invoice first, then raised two real-world complications: customers with multiple workshops and multiple concurrent projects. Three-level party model (customer → location → deal) answers both structurally instead of patching later; one extra table now is cheap vs backfilling location semantics onto existing deals later.

cards.title: P5 — Stock & equipment: custody-only, opt-in tracking, shortfall debts, temp products, rename/merge-safe
cards.description: Phase 5 scope after six user follow-ups. (1) Single DB, single `products` catalog; per-product TRACKING REGIME, `untracked` DEFAULT (small parts = catalog entries only, no ledger/counts/movements); `qty` opt-in loose ledger; `serialized` identity tracking (rows live forever, scrap transition only). QP-CRM = custody of machines + debts between machines, NOT inventory value (audit software stays the counting truth). (2) Custody-first movements, nullable doc ref + fixed reason list. (3) Coverage loop: reservations with "for whom", first-class POs (derived status), ATP view over tracked products. (4) Fleet vans as internal custodians (NOT customer rows). (5) Donor parts as SHORTFALLS (equipment_shortfalls: device, part, taken-for, PO ref, closed_at) — two-tap mechanic flow, incomplete-device flag, orders-needed hook, auto-close on replacement receipt; timeline-note fallback allowed but loses reminders. (6) TEMP PRODUCTS app-wide: every reference is id (nullable FK) + text snapshot (name/desc/photo) — quotation already does this (offer_items.product_id NULL + item_name); warehouse movements & equipment registrations accept temp products (ad-hoc part/device without catalog row), one-click "make real product" promotes snapshot → catalog row and back-fills references. RENAME without breakage: all modules resolve names by id at read time — renaming edits one master row. MERGE 2-or-5-into-1: `product_aliases` (alias_id → canonical_id, UNIQUE alias, no chains); old ids keep resolving through the alias map; duplicate-suspect view + re-point merge tool; same machinery reusable for customers/locations later. Issued documents keep issuance-time snapshots — rename/merge never rewrites history.
cards.rationale: User's final two requirements: (a) the quotation temp-product must exist in the warehouse too (one-off parts/devices shouldn't force catalog rows), and (b) the DB being "just links" must make renames and N-into-1 merges non-breaking. Both follow from one convention (id + snapshot + alias map) that is cheap to adopt on day one and painful to retrofit — recording it before P4/P5 schemas are written.
cards.rejected: Foreign-key-name lookups everywhere (name as key) — rejected: makes renames break references, the exact opposite of the requirement. Auto-updating historical document lines on rename/merge — rejected: issued offers/invoices are legal records; they keep issuance-time snapshots. Cascade-rewriting all references at merge time with no alias map — rejected: irreversible and lossy; alias map keeps old ids resolvable forever. Fancy dedup engines — rejected: alias map + duplicate-suspect view + manual confirm is enough and stays understandable.
